records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא־אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל־בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי־אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH to Noah, go, you and all your household, into the ark, for you I have seen righteous before me in this generation.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Noah, "Go into the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen that you are righteous before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} among the people of this generation.

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Noah, "Go, you and all your household, into the ark, for I have seen that you [are] righteous before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this generation.

R.1: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Noah, "Go into the boat with all your family. Of all the people living now, you are the one I see doing what is right.

decisions.choice: I have seen you righteous before me: God's own verdict on Noah
decisions.reason: The narrator called Noah righteous (6:9); now God says it himself. "Before me" means in God's sight, by his judgment. Noah's household is saved with him.

decisions.choice: this generation: the people living at that time
decisions.reason: A generation is the people of one time. "This generation" stands for the corrupt world of 6:11-12.

decisions.choice: before me (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, so "me" takes the deity pronoun setting.

records.heading: The flood

records.source: מִכֹּ֣ל׀הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה תִּֽקַּח־לְךָ֛ שִׁבְעָ֥ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָ֡ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א טְהֹרָ֥ה הִ֛וא שְׁנַ֖יִם אִ֥ישׁ וְאִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Of all the animal[s] the clean you will take for yourself seven seven, a male and its female; and of the animal[s] which not clean it [is], two, a male and its female;
pieces: Take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate, and one pair of every kind of animal that is not clean, a male and its mate,

L.2: Of every clean animal you will take for yourself seven [and] seven, a male and its mate; and of the animals that [are] not clean, two, a male and its mate;

R.2: Take with you seven pairs of every kind of animal that is clean, a male and a female of each. Take one pair, a male and a female, of every kind of animal that is not clean.

decisions.choice: seven seven: seven pairs
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats a number to mean "so many each". Since each is "a male and its mate", seven seven most likely means seven pairs, though it can be read as seven animals.

decisions.choice: clean and not clean: animals fit or unfit for sacrifice and food
decisions.reason: "Clean" animals were those fit to be offered to God and, later, eaten (Leviticus 11). The distinction is assumed here, before the law of Moses. The extra clean animals provide for the sacrifice after the flood (8:20). 6:19-20 gave the general rule, two of every kind; this verse adds to it.

decisions.choice: a male and its mate: literally "a man and his wife"
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses the words for man and woman, husband and wife, for a male and female animal.

records.source: גַּ֣ם מֵע֧וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם שִׁבְעָ֥ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה זָכָ֣ר וּנְקֵבָ֑ה לְחַיּ֥וֹת זֶ֖רַע עַל־פְּנֵ֥י כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Also of [the] bird[s] of the heavens seven seven, male and female, to keep alive offspring on [the] face of all the earth.
pieces: and seven pairs of every kind of bird of the sky, male and female, to keep their kinds alive on the face of all the earth.

L.3: also of the birds of the heavens seven [and] seven, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the face of all the earth.

R.3: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird, males and females, so that each kind can live on across the earth.

decisions.choice: to keep offspring alive: so that each kind continues
decisions.reason: "Offspring" (seed) means the next generations. The purpose is that each kind of creature will fill the earth again after the flood.

records.source: כִּי֩ לְיָמִ֨ים ע֜וֹד שִׁבְעָ֗ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ מַמְטִ֣יר עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָ֑יְלָה וּמָחִ֗יתִי אֶֽת־כָּל־הַיְקוּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: For in seven more days I [am] causing rain on the earth forty day[s] and forty night[s], and I will wipe out every living thing that I have made from on [the] face of the ground.
pieces: In seven days I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living thing I have made."

L.4: For in seven more days I will send rain on the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out every living thing that I have made from the face of the ground."

R.4: In seven days I will make it rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe out every living thing I made."

decisions.choice: forty days and forty nights: a long, set time
decisions.reason: Forty is a common number in the Bible for a full period of testing or judgment: Moses on the mountain (Exodus 24:18), Elijah's journey (1 Kings 19:8), Jesus in the wilderness (Matthew 4:2).

decisions.choice: every living thing: every being that exists
decisions.reason: The word, rare in the Bible, means whatever stands or exists, here every living creature.

records.source: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And did Noah according to all that commanded him YHWH.
pieces: Noah did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded him.

L.5: And Noah did according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded him.

R.5: Noah did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told him to do.

decisions.choice: Noah did all that the LORD commanded: as in 6:22
decisions.reason: The words repeat 6:22. Noah's obedience is the thread through the account (7:9, 16).

records.source: וְנֹ֕חַ בֶּן־שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וְהַמַּבּ֣וּל הָיָ֔ה מַ֖יִם עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And Noah [was] a son of six hundred year[s], and the flood was, water on the earth.
pieces: Noah was 600 years old when the flood waters came on the earth.

L.6: And Noah [was] 600 years old when the flood came, water on the earth.

R.6: Noah was 600 years old when the flood came and covered the earth with water.

decisions.choice: a son of 600 years: 600 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives age as "a son of" so many years (as in 5:32).

records.source: וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי־בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֵ֥י הַמַּבּֽוּל׃
records.gloss: And went Noah and his sons and his wife and the wives of his sons with him into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.
pieces: And Noah and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives went into the ark to escape the waters of the flood.

L.7: And Noah went, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him, into the ark because of the waters of the flood.

R.7: Noah went into the boat with his wife, his sons and their wives, to escape the flood waters.

decisions.choice: because of the waters: to escape them
decisions.reason: The phrase means "from before" the waters: they enter the ark to get away from them.

records.source: מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ הַטְּהוֹרָ֔ה וּמִן־הַ֨בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵינֶ֖נָּה טְהֹרָ֑ה וּמִ֨ן־הָע֔וֹף וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־רֹמֵ֖שׂ עַל־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Of the animal[s] the clean, and of the animal[s] which not it [was] clean, and of the bird[s], and all that creeps on the ground,
pieces: Clean animals and animals that are not clean, birds and every creature that moves along the ground

L.8: Of the clean animals, and of the animals that [were] not clean, and of the birds, and of everything that creeps on the ground,

R.8: Clean animals and animals that were not clean, birds, and small creatures that crawl on the ground

records.source: שְׁנַ֨יִם שְׁנַ֜יִם בָּ֧אוּ אֶל־נֹ֛חַ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֖ה זָכָ֣ר וּנְקֵבָ֑ה כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־נֹֽחַ׃
records.gloss: two two they came to Noah into the ark, male and female, as had commanded God Noah.
pieces: came to Noah in pairs and went into the ark, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.

L.9: two [and] two they came to Noah into the ark, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.

R.9: came to Noah in pairs, a male and a female, and went into the boat, just as God had commanded Noah.

decisions.choice: two two: in pairs
decisions.reason: As with "seven seven" in verse 2, the doubled number means "two by two". It describes how they came, in pairs, not the total of each kind (verse 2 says seven pairs of clean animals).

decisions.choice: they came to Noah: the animals come of themselves
decisions.reason: As God said in 6:20, the animals come to Noah; he does not gather them.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֖י לְשִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וּמֵ֣י הַמַּבּ֔וּל הָי֖וּ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And it was after the seven days, and [the] waters of the flood were on the earth.
pieces: After the seven days the flood waters came on the earth.

L.10: And it happened after the seven days that the waters of the flood came on the earth.

R.10: Seven days later, the flood waters came over the earth.

decisions.choice: after the seven days: as God said in verse 4
decisions.reason: God's word in verse 4 is fulfilled to the day. Seven days also recalls the week of creation now being undone.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי־נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה־עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל־מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: In [the] year of six hundred year[s] of [the] life of Noah, in the second month, on [the] seventeenth day of the month, on this day, were split open all [the] springs of [the] deep great, and [the] windows of the heavens were opened.
pieces: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, on that very day all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.

L.11: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the heavens were opened.

R.11: When Noah was 600 years old, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the springs deep under the earth burst open. The windows of the sky opened, and the rain poured down.

decisions.choice: the springs of the great deep, the windows of the heavens: creation undone
decisions.reason: The deep (1:2) and the waters above the vault (1:7) were held in their places at creation. Now the springs below burst out and the windows above open, and the waters return over the earth, as if the separation of the second day were being undone.

decisions.choice: windows of the heavens: openings for the waters above
decisions.reason: The word means a window or lattice (Hosea 13:3). In the picture of the world of chapter 1, the waters above the vault pour through its windows (8:2; compare 2 Kings 7:2).

decisions.choice: the second month, the seventeenth day: a dated event
decisions.reason: The flood is dated by Noah's life, like a record of events. The text does not say which calendar it uses, so it is not clear in which season the month fell.

decisions.choice: floodgates
decisions.reason: Balanced says "floodgates" for what the windows do (m2); Literal and Readable keep "windows".

decisions.choice: and the rain poured down
decisions.reason: Readable says what the opening of the windows meant, as verse 12 goes on to tell.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֥י הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: And was the rain on the earth forty day[s] and forty night[s].
pieces: And rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights.

L.12: And the rain was on the earth forty days and forty nights.

R.12: It rained on the earth for forty days and forty nights.

records.source: בְּעֶ֨צֶם הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ בָּ֣א נֹ֔חַ וְשֵׁם־וְחָ֥ם וָיֶ֖פֶת בְּנֵי־נֹ֑חַ וְאֵ֣שֶׁת נֹ֗חַ וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת נְשֵֽׁי־בָנָ֛יו אִתָּ֖ם אֶל־הַתֵּבָֽה׃
records.gloss: On this very day went Noah, and Shem and Ham and Japheth, [the] sons of Noah, and [the] wife of Noah, and [the] three wives of his sons with them, into the ark,
pieces: On that very day Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, together with his wife and the wives of his three sons, went into the ark,

L.13: On that very day Noah went, and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark,

R.13: On that same day Noah went into the boat with his wife, his sons Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their three wives.

decisions.choice: on that very day: on the exact day
decisions.reason: "The bone of the day" means the very same day; the phrase marks a solemn moment (17:23, 26; Exodus 12:17).

records.source: הֵ֜מָּה וְכָל־הַֽחַיָּ֣ה לְמִינָ֗הּ וְכָל־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ וְכָל־הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וְכָל־הָע֣וֹף לְמִינֵ֔הוּ כֹּ֖ל צִפּ֥וֹר כָּל־כָּנָֽף׃
records.gloss: they, and every animal according to its kind, and all the livestock according to its kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, every bird, every wing.
pieces: they and every wild animal according to its kind, all the livestock according to their kinds, every creature that moves along the ground according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, everything with wings.

L.14: they and every animal according to its kind, and all the livestock according to their kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, every bird, every winged [creature].

R.14: With them went every kind of wild animal, every kind of farm animal, every kind of small creature that crawls on the ground, and every kind of bird, everything that has wings.

decisions.choice: according to its kind: the list of chapter 1
decisions.reason: The list follows the creatures of the fifth and sixth days, each "according to its kind" (1:21-25). Every kind God made is brought into safety.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־נֹ֖חַ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֑ה שְׁנַ֤יִם שְׁנַ֨יִם֙ מִכָּל־הַבָּשָׂ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־בּ֖וֹ ר֥וּחַ חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And they came to Noah into the ark, two two of all flesh in which [was the] breath of life.
pieces: They came to Noah and went into the ark in pairs, of every creature that has the breath of life.

L.15: And they came to Noah into the ark, two [and] two of all flesh in which [was] the breath of life.

R.15: Pairs of every living creature that breathes came to Noah and went into the boat.

records.source: וְהַבָּאִ֗ים זָכָ֨ר וּנְקֵבָ֤ה מִכָּל־בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֔אוּ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בַּֽעֲדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And those coming, male and female of all flesh they came, as had commanded him God. And shut YHWH behind him.
pieces: Those that went in were male and female of every creature, as God had commanded Noah. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shut him in.

L.16: And those that came, male and female of all flesh, came as God had commanded him. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shut [the door] behind him.

R.16: The animals came in, male and female of every kind, as God had told Noah. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} closed the door behind him.

decisions.choice: the LORD shut him in: God himself closes the ark
decisions.reason: Noah does not close the door; the LORD does. It is an act of protection: the ark's one door is shut by God, and Noah is kept safe inside. The narrator uses the name the LORD here, where the verse has just said "God".

decisions.choice: shut [the door] behind him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "shut behind him"; Literal brackets "the door".

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֧י הַמַּבּ֛וּל אַרְבָּעִ֥ים י֖וֹם עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּרְבּ֣וּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־הַתֵּבָ֔ה וַתָּ֖רָם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And was the flood forty day[s] on the earth, and increased the waters and lifted up the ark, and it rose from on the earth.
pieces: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth. The waters rose and lifted the ark, and it floated high above the earth.

L.17: And the flood was forty days on the earth, and the waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the earth.

R.17: For forty days the flood kept getting deeper. The water lifted the boat up off the ground, high above the earth.

decisions.choice: increased ... lifted ... rose: the story slows as the waters climb
decisions.reason: Verses 17-20 repeat "the waters increased" in rising steps, with more emphasis each time ("greatly", "very greatly"), so that the reader feels the flood rise.

records.source: וַיִּגְבְּר֥וּ הַמַּ֛יִם וַיִּרְבּ֥וּ מְאֹ֖ד עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ הַתֵּבָ֖ה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And prevailed the waters and increased greatly on the earth, and went the ark on [the] face of the waters.
pieces: The waters swelled and rose higher and higher on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.

L.18: And the waters prevailed and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark went on the face of the waters.

R.18: The water kept rising higher and higher, and the boat floated on top of it.

decisions.choice: prevailed: grew strong, overpowered
decisions.reason: The verb (gavar) means to be strong or to win. The waters overpower the earth (verses 18, 19, 20, 24).

records.source: וְהַמַּ֗יִם גָּֽבְר֛וּ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹ֖ד עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיְכֻסּ֗וּ כָּל־הֶֽהָרִים֙ הַגְּבֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־תַּ֖חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And the waters prevailed very very on the earth, and were covered all the mountains the high that [were] under all the heavens.
pieces: The waters rose so high on the earth that all the high mountains under the whole sky were covered.

L.19: And the waters prevailed exceedingly on the earth, and all the high mountains that [were] under all the heavens were covered.

R.19: The water rose so high that it covered all the high mountains under the sky.

decisions.choice: all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered: the whole world as the account sees it
alternatives: a flood over the whole region known to the writer
decisions.reason: The account describes the flood as covering the whole earth, with "all" repeated through the chapter, and it is the judgment on all flesh (6:13). Readers differ on whether it describes a flood over the whole globe or over the world as its first readers knew it; the text itself speaks of everything under the heavens.

decisions.choice: very very: exceedingly
decisions.reason: The doubled word is the strongest way Hebrew says "very much".

records.source: חֲמֵ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה גָּבְר֖וּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְכֻסּ֖וּ הֶהָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Fifteen cubit[s] upward prevailed the waters, and were covered the mountains.
pieces: The waters rose {{units:more than 20 feet|fifteen cubits}} above them, and the mountains were covered.

L.20: Fifteen cubits upward the waters prevailed, and the mountains were covered.

R.20: The water was {{units:more than 20 feet|fifteen cubits}} deep above the tops of the mountains.

decisions.choice: fifteen cubits upward: above the mountains
decisions.reason: Fifteen cubits is about 22 feet (7 meters). It is most naturally read as the depth of water above the highest mountains. Fifteen cubits is also half the height of the ark (6:15), so it would float clear of them.

decisions.choice: more than 20 feet; with the Measures setting, fifteen cubits
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give modern measures by default (22.5 feet, rounded), and cubits as the setting's alternative; Literal keeps cubits.

records.source: וַיִּגְוַ֞ע כָּל־בָּשָׂ֣ר׀הָרֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ בָּע֤וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבַ֣חַיָּ֔ה וּבְכָל־הַשֶּׁ֖רֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵ֣ץ עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל הָאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And died all flesh that creeps on the earth, among the bird[s] and among the livestock and among the animal[s] and among every swarming thing that swarms on the earth, and all humankind.
pieces: Every living creature that moved on the earth died: birds, livestock, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all {{gender:people|mankind}}.

L.21: And all flesh that moves on the earth died, birds and livestock and wild animals and every swarming thing that swarms on the earth, and all {{gender:humankind|men}}.

R.21: Every living thing on earth died: birds, farm animals, wild animals, all the small creatures, and all {{gender:people|mankind}}.

decisions.choice: died: perished
decisions.reason: The verb (gava) means to breathe one's last, to expire. It is the word God used in 6:17.

decisions.choice: and all humankind: last in the list
decisions.reason: Human beings, the cause of the judgment, come last in the list of the dead, as they were made last (1:26).

decisions.choice: humankind / people; with the traditional setting, men or mankind
decisions.reason: The word means human beings of both sexes, so the default is inclusive.

records.source: כֹּ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁמַת־ר֨וּחַ חַיִּ֜ים בְּאַפָּ֗יו מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֶּחָֽרָבָ֖ה מֵֽתוּ׃
records.gloss: All that [had the] breath of [the] spirit of life in its nostrils, of all that [was] on the dry land, died.
pieces: Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.

L.22: Everything that [had] the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils, of all that [was] on the dry land, died.

R.22: Everything on land that breathed air died.

decisions.choice: the breath of life in its nostrils: the words of 2:7
decisions.reason: The breath God breathed into the man's nostrils (2:7) is taken back. The words gather up the breath of 2:7 and the spirit of life of 6:17.

decisions.choice: dry land: the land, as against the sea
decisions.reason: Only land creatures are named. Sea creatures are not said to die; the account is about life on the dry land God called out of the waters (1:9-10).

records.source: וַיִּ֜מַח אֶֽת־כָּל־הַיְק֣וּם׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה מֵאָדָ֤ם עַד־בְּהֵמָה֙ עַד־רֶ֨מֶשׂ֙ וְעַד־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמָּח֖וּ מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִשָּׁ֧אֶראַךְ־נֹ֛חַ וַֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he wiped out every living thing that [was] on [the] face of the ground, from humankind to animal[s], to creeping thing[s], and to [the] bird[s] of the heavens, and they were wiped out from the earth, and was left only Noah and those who [were] with him in the ark.
pieces: So every living thing on the face of the earth was wiped out, from {{gender:people|man}} to animals, creatures that move along the ground and birds of the sky. They were wiped from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark.

L.23: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wiped out every living thing that [was] on the face of the ground, from {{gender:humankind|man}} to animals, to creeping things, and to the birds of the heavens; and they were wiped out from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those that [were] with him in the ark.

R.23: God wiped out every living thing on earth: {{gender:people|man}}, animals, small creatures and birds. They were all gone. Only Noah and those with him in the boat were left alive.

decisions.choice: he wiped out: as God said in 6:7
decisions.reason: The words of 6:7 and 7:4 are carried out exactly, with the same list from humankind to the birds.

decisions.choice: only Noah was left: a remnant
decisions.reason: The verb "be left" gives the later word for the remnant God keeps when he judges (Isaiah 10:20-22). Through the few left, life goes on.

decisions.choice: every living thing ... was wiped out
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the sentence in the passive, since the next words say "they were wiped out"; God is the one who acts, as Literal and Readable say.

records.source: וַיִּגְבְּר֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And prevailed the waters on the earth fifty and a hundred day[s].
pieces: The waters flooded the earth for 150 days.

L.24: And the waters prevailed on the earth 150 days.

R.24: The water stayed high over the earth for 150 days.

decisions.choice: prevailed: stayed at their height
decisions.reason: The 150 days count from the start of the flood (compare 8:3-4, where the waters go down after 150 days and the ark comes to rest five months after 7:11).
